title: Adaptive Patching for High-resolution Image Segmentation with Transformers
problem: Transformer models have quadratic compute and memory costs in attention mechanisms. For high-resolution images like pathology slides, small patch sizes necessary for segmentation quality become computationally prohibitive.
motivation: Transformers are increasingly used for image segmentation tasks, but their quadratic attention complexity prevents application to high-resolution medical imaging data.
method: Inspired by Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR) techniques from HPC, the approach adaptively divides images into patches based on image details during preprocessing, reducing the number of patches fed to the transformer encoder. This achieves orders-of-magnitude patch reduction with negligible overhead and integrates seamlessly with any transformer model without requiring architectural modification.
key_novelty: Applying Adaptive Mesh Refinement principles to image patch generation for transformers to overcome quadratic attention scaling on high-resolution images.
contributions: Adaptive patching method that reduces token count by orders of magnitude while maintaining compatibility with any attention-based model
Achieves 6.9x geomean speedup on high-resolution images up to 64K² resolution using up to 2,048 GPUs
Demonstrates superior segmentation quality compared to state-of-the-art models on real-world pathology datasets
Provides negligible-overhead preprocessing that requires no model retraining or architectural changes
primary_theme: Adaptive mesh refinement for efficient transformer inference on high-resolution images
